about: Sensitivity checks for the Round 1 pressure index. The primary (submitted) lists are the exclusions-on lists. Nothing here changes the primary method or the primary lists. Regenerate with `node sensitivity.mjs` from the data folder.

primaryCheck.description: Primary (submitted) lists as computed here (scoring.mjs on analysis_data.json, player exclusions on, 60 balls / 8 matches).

poolSizes.note: Eligible players per format-season pool, exclusions on (the submitted setting), 60 pressure balls / 8 matches / 60 ordinary balls. A pool with 10 or fewer players is flagged thin. Each player is standardised (z-scores) only against the others in the same pool.

method.leaveOneOut: Drop one eligible player of the same kind (all his records as a batter, or as a bowler), re-rate everyone with scoring.mjs, record the rank of every primary top-10 player other than the dropped one. A dropped player ranked above a top-10 player lifts that rank by one, so the best rank here is mechanical; the worst rank and the exit count carry the information.
method.bootstrap: 1000 resamples. Within each player-format-season group, the player-match records are drawn with replacement to the same count (a match-level cluster bootstrap), then everything is re-rated with scoring.mjs including the 60-ball / 8-match gate. This measures sampling noise in a player's own results (the primary top-10 players have 93 to 684 pressure balls) together with its effect on the pool z-scores, so it is a wider test than pool size alone; poolDeletion is the pool-only test.
method.poolDeletion: 1000 runs. In each run a random 20% of the eligible players who are not in the primary top 10 are removed (6 batters, 14 bowlers), then everything is re-rated. The top-10 players' own data is untouched, so this isolates how much the make-up of the pools matters.
method.fragilityRule: Share of runs with the player in the top 10: fragile below 50%, moderate 50% to under 80%, stable 80% or more. `fragility` uses the bootstrap share (a player's own sampling noise and the pools together); `poolCompositionFragility` uses the random pool-deletion share (only who else is in the pools changes).

otherAlternative.assumption: Primary: an `other` delivery is an illegal ball (not one of the six legal balls) and the bowler is charged one penalty run, as for a no-ball; the run also counts in the innings score used for the required rate. Alternative shown here: still an illegal ball, but no penalty run is charged to the bowler or added to the innings score.

exclusionsOn.scenario: exclusions on, `other` = illegal ball, no penalty run

exclusionsOff.scenario: no exclusions, `other` = illegal ball, no penalty run

noExclusionAlternative.note: The alternative to the submitted lists: same method and thresholds, with no player exclusions applied (five of the six IPL retirees are switched off here; the sixth stays excluded in every setting). Columns are the same as the primary tables; versusPrimary compares with the submitted (exclusions on) lists.
noExclusionAlternative.scenario: alternative: no exclusions, `other` = illegal ball + 1 penalty run

alternative: no exclusions, `other` = illegal ball + 1 penalty run

otherEvidence.source: ball_by_ball.csv, rows of the IPL matches that are rated (2022 to 2026, innings 1 to 4)

overLength.note: Legal balls in an over = rows in that over minus the rows known to be illegal (wide, Overstep), and minus the `other` rows in the "illegal" case. The last over of each innings is excluded because it can be cut short.

runMarginCheck.note: Matches decided by runs, with no byes, leg-byes, penalty rows, super over or revised overs, where the winning margin should equal innings 1 total minus innings 2 total (bat runs + 1 per wide and Overstep). The method is first checked on matches that have no `other` row.
runMarginCheck.verdict: low power: exact reconstruction fails in many matches that have no `other` row (the data holds no innings totals and no overthrow, bye or leg-bye runs), so it cannot decide the penalty question alone; the decisive tests are in decisiveTests

decisiveTests.source: other_evidence_data.json (node other_evidence.mjs --write); IPL matches 2022 to 2026 in ball_by_ball.csv

interpretations.b: illegal ball, no penalty run (alternative, otherAlternative)

decisiveTests.decision: keep a (illegal ball, +1 penalty run): c is rejected by the free-hit, over-length and 120-ball tests; the regression coefficient for `other` has a 95% CI containing 1 and excluding 0. analyze.mjs and analysis_data.json are unchanged.

inScopeEffect.note: Pressure deliveries in the IPL matches with the penalty run (primary) and without it.

summary: 123 rows have extras_type 'other'. extras1_runs is 5 on 123 rows; for wide it is 2, for Overstep 1, for ordinary balls 6.
Batter runs are recorded on 63 of the 123 'other' rows (16 sixes, 20 fours); on Overstep rows 149 of 257; wides never carry batter runs (0 of 3552).
2 'other' rows carry a wicket: 2 RunOut. For Overstep rows: 3 RunOut.

120 overs contain an 'other' row. If 'other' were a legal ball, 113 of them would have more than six legal balls (100 of the 100 that are not the last over of an innings); treated as illegal, 113 have exactly six (100 of 100 not-last overs). Overs with no 'other' row have exactly six in 100.0% of 13234 finished overs.

No row says how many runs the 'other' extra is worth: 'runs' is the batter's runs on every extras type, so the +1 penalty is a rule-based assumption (a no-ball costs the bowler one run), not something read from a column. Exact run-margin reconstruction has low power (1 of 3 calibration matches reproduce the margin; 0 match with an 'other' row qualifies). The decisive tests are in decisiveTests: keep a (illegal ball, +1 penalty run): c is rejected by the free-hit, over-length and 120-ball tests; the regression coefficient for `other` has a 95% CI containing 1 and excluding 0. analyze.mjs and analysis_data.json are unchanged.
In the in-scope data the penalty run adds 26 pressure deliveries (37926 to 37952).

exclusionFlip.summary: One line in scoring.mjs switches the player exclusions off. The submitted lists use the exclusions. The change is `true` to `false` on the APPLY_PLAYER_EXCLUSIONS line.
exclusionFlip.checkDescription: sensitivity.mjs applies this exact edit to a copy of scoring.mjs in memory and confirms the batter, bowler and all-rounder lists equal the noExclusionAlternative lists in this file.
exclusionFlip.whatTheEditDoes: Keeps the format and season filters and drops the player exclusion that touches IPL players for five of the six retirees (Pollard, Bravo, Rayudu, Karthik, Ashwin); the sixth stays excluded. The dashboard imports scoring.mjs, so it shows the no-exclusion lists as soon as the line is changed. The text lists of the submitted names (the report, README.md, index.html) do not change by themselves.
exclusionFlip.analysisDataNeedsRegenerating: No. The exclusions are applied in scoring.mjs after analysis_data.json is built, so do not run analyze.mjs for this change.
commands: 1. In scoring.mjs change `const APPLY_PLAYER_EXCLUSIONS = true;` to `const APPLY_PLAYER_EXCLUSIONS = false;`.

2. node sensitivity.mjs --print-top10   (prints the top-10 batters and bowlers that scoring.mjs now gives; they must equal noExclusionAlternative.batters.top10 and noExclusionAlternative.bowlers.top10 in sensitivity_data.json, which holds the full metrics).

3. Do not run `node sensitivity.mjs` or `node charts.mjs` without arguments while the line says false: both describe the submitted exclusions-on lists and stop with an error. Change the line back to true before rebuilding sensitivity_data.json or the charts.

4. Report: methodology_report.md, methodology_report.html and methodology_report.pdf are written by hand (the PDF is the html printed to PDF). The no-exclusion lists with full metrics are already in the report section "Alternative: top 10 lists with no exclusions". To submit them, move those tables into the top-10 section, update the exclusion text, and print the PDF again.

5. Static text that also mentions the exclusions: README.md, index.html (method step 06) and the exclusion paragraphs in the report. The Unstop dropdown entries must be changed to the no-exclusion names.
